# Retrospective, PR 12763

## What worked

Bounded read-only security intake preceded fresh reviewer launches. Exact head/base/merge-base and empty discussion were recorded. Fresh Claude Code Opus 5.5 High and Pi GPT 6 Sol Xhigh investigated independently; peer conclusions were shared only after both finals were saved. Matching compositor-release source answered API questions without host UI access. The negative test control exposed an interpreter invocation flaw that a clean head run alone missed. Raw child stderr and exit receipts, rather than aggregate pass labels, made the test note defensible. No finding quota was used.

## Deviations retained and corrected

- Opus used long-format ownership-resolving directory listings, contrary to numeric-metadata policy, and incidentally saw peer `assignment.md` metadata. No peer contents/conclusions were read. Future inventories must be names-only, numeric `ls -lan`, or numeric stat APIs. Do not repeat the listing for audit.
- Opus's two fixtures asserted private case roots but omitted explicit assertions for mkdir subpaths, copy destinations, sed temporary paths and here-document temporary paths. Some summary/read/time producers were unchecked; some expected statuses were broad. Coordinator read both complete fixtures and requested a separate correction; `reviewers/fable/follow-up-audit.md` retracts full-guard wording and the unrecorded timeout-124 inference. Original fixtures, plans and sealed bundles remain unchanged. No elapsed-time or summary-total claim is accepted. Source and directly inspected exact error/exit controls still support the narrow Lua invocation claim; all relevant setup receipts show success. No rerun was added merely to repair presentation of valid source-backed evidence.
- Sol's guessed docs URL failed (404) and an unchecked byte-count followed. Both are excluded. A broad source-discovery result was persisted by the Pi harness at `/tmp/pi-bash-b49ac493737ad6a1.log`, outside the assignment, containing public upstream source and local source path names, not credentials. Native history is preserved, not deleted. Subsequent source fetches retained separate status/error receipts. Avoid speculative fetch paths and bound discovery output.
- Source materialization included one failed coordinator lookup of nonexistent test/run.sh, retained in intake. The actual test/shell runner was then inspected. This was source acquisition, not execution or evidence of missing functionality.
- review.py internally gates its git archive producer but does not retain a separate stderr/exit file per such internal producer. Evidence claims are limited to inspected scoped files and raw command results, not complete producer instrumentation.

## Corrected local handoff requirement

Before any further fixture is approved, enumerate every final write path and each invoked callee, including mkdir descendants, copy files, sed/compiler/helper temporaries, done markers and summary appends. Resolve/assert each destination beneath the private writable root before its first write; a parent assertion alone is insufficient. Declare exact expected child status and expected output before execution. Gate every producer independently, including date/read/count helpers; do not infer nested child status from a wrapper or timeout-shaped delay. Fail the affected case on setup errors. Inventory archive members before extraction. Retain direct streams from launch and use unique receipts. Use numeric metadata only and bounded source discovery. This supplements the already supplied full corrections without retroactively claiming earlier compliance.

## Remaining limits and cleanup

No native compositor or Toolbox experiment and no whole-suite run. No desktop slots, background fixture processes or long-lived servers were created. Completed namespace runs ended, ephemeral private tmpfs trees vanished. Source checkouts, fetched sources, sealed evidence and native agent histories remain. Reviewers report no owned runtime PIDs requiring cleanup; no global process search was performed. Reviewer panes are preserved. No confirmed infrastructure bug requiring a shared-tool edit was established.

The deviations are private audit information. Current public claims remain source-backed and corroborated by exact raw results; process compliance is recorded false rather than overclaimed. No publication by the coordinator.
comment:
No production issue found in the reviewed scope at `298ee3e77206`; one test-only improvement is noted below.

**Verified:** The targeted Lua mock checks pass, covering off-screen recovery, partial visibility, negative monitor origins, scaled/rotated bounds, delayed guards and reload. The API calls and move-then-center ordering also match Hyprland v0.56.2 source.

```text
Floating XWayland Toolbox, at open or reload
  → delayed checks at 150 and 750 ms
  → closed, hidden, unmapped, tiled or replaced: leave alone
  → intersects any monitor: leave alone
  → entirely off-screen, active workspace available: move, center, raise
```

This describes the inspected logic and mocked behavior, not a live Toolbox run.

**Optional test improvement:** In [`jetbrains-toolbox-window-test.sh:6`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/298ee3e77206e68d7977dc9648ad806c0df016bb/test/shell.d/jetbrains-toolbox-window-test.sh#L6), use `timeout 10s lua - <<'LUA' || exit 1`. With the tested Lua 5.5.1 interpreter, removing the stable-ID guard prints an assertion traceback but the current test still exits 0; adding `-` makes that same assertion failure exit 1, while the unmodified head still passes. This lets the shell suite detect failing checks rather than relying on stderr inspection.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review against Hyprland v0.56.2 and isolated Lua mock checks with diagnostic controls. No live compositor, XWayland or Toolbox run; actual placement and application timing remain unverified.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, followed by evidence reconciliation and a separate Astra Medium editorial check.
